name: Measurement-instrument validation pass (four self-defeating shapes)
description: Before any number is read, validate the INSTRUMENT that produced it. This is not a detector fixture and needs no broken state to be constructed: it inspects the instrument's own construction for four shapes that are known to defeat themselves - a run that reports two things which cannot both be true; a probe whose pattern matches its OWN command line; a comparator comparing two different things; and a harness that does not suit its target. Only then does it run a known-present control, because a zero from an unvalidated instrument is not a measurement. An invalid instrument means the measurement is DISCARDED, never adjusted.

measurement.description: The number or verdict about to drive a decision, verbatim as reported.

instrument_command.description: The exact command, query or code that produced the measurement. The four shape checks read THIS, not the number.

instrument_output.description: The instrument's full output including exit code, so a self-contradiction inside one run is visible.

expected_range.description: Optional prior. A measurement outside it is not wrong, but it raises the bar on the control.

known_present_item.description: An item the instrument MUST find. Without this a zero is uninterpretable.

consequence.description: Contraindication switch: at 'trivial' the pass is skipped, since validating a number nobody acts on is waste.

instrument-auditor.description: Reads the instrument's construction - not its result - looking for the four known self-defeating shapes.

control-runner.description: Runs the instrument against a known-present item and, where a broken state can be built, against that too.

stages.title: Shape 1 - does ONE run report two things that cannot both be true

work_unit.title: Detect a self-contradiction inside a single instrument run
work_unit.question_or_target: Read the instrument's own output for two claims that cannot both hold - the measured archetype is `grep -c pat || echo 0`, which prints 0 AND exits 1 so the fallback also fires, yielding '0\n0' that compares unequal to '0'.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: reading a construction for a known defect shape is judgement work, not a regex

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the two mutually exclusive claims quoted verbatim from the one run, with the construct that produced them
tests_required: the `grep -c pat || echo 0` construct is FLAGGED
both-states control: a plain `grep -c pat` with the exit code handled is NOT flagged, proving the check discriminates rather than flagging every grep
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the control-runner, who must be able to reproduce the contradiction from the recorded construct
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7401 emitted only when a verdict of self-contradictory or clean is recorded with the quoted evidence; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7401 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: a shape check is a read, and re-reading the same text is not a second signal
work_unit.mechanism: static inspection of one run's output for mutually exclusive claims

stages.title: A self-contradicting run halts the analysis - fix the instrument first
Shape 2 - does the probe's pattern appear in its OWN command line

work_unit.title: Detect a probe that matches itself
work_unit.question_or_target: Check whether the search pattern occurs in the probe's own command line, which makes a dead process report ACTIVE. The decisive tell is that the reported CreationDate equals the probe's own run time.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the tell is a timestamp coincidence a human reads at a glance and a regex misses

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the pattern, the probe's own command line, and a comparison of the reported creation time against the probe's start time
tests_required: a process probe whose pattern is in its own command line is FLAGGED, citing the equal timestamps
both-states control: a probe that excludes its own pid is NOT flagged
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7402 emitted only when a self-match verdict is recorded with the timestamp comparison shown; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7402 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: a shape check reads a construction, and re-reading the same text is not a second signal
work_unit.mechanism: pattern-in-own-command-line detection with the timestamp-coincidence tell

stages.title: Shape 3 - is the comparator comparing like with like

work_unit.title: Detect a comparator that compares two different things
work_unit.question_or_target: Establish that the two sides of the comparison are the same kind of object - the measured failure compared record.py against stubscan.py and reported DRIFT, which of course they exhibit because they are different files.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: deciding whether two operands are comparable requires knowing what each IS

work_unit.evidence_requirement: both operands named with their type and provenance, and a statement of why they are or are not the same kind of object
tests_required: comparing two differently-named source files and calling the difference DRIFT is FLAGGED
both-states control: comparing the same logical file across two revisions is NOT flagged
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7403 emitted only when both operands are typed and a comparability verdict is recorded; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7403 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: an operand-identity check is a read, not an operation that can transiently fail
work_unit.mechanism: operand-identity check on the comparison's two sides

stages.title: Shape 4 - does the harness suit the target, and is the exit code DECODED

work_unit.title: Detect a harness mismatch and an undecoded exit code
work_unit.question_or_target: Check the runner suits the target and that every exit code is decoded rather than assumed - a standalone script under pytest yields `INTERNALERROR: SystemExit: 0` which reads as a failing suite, and 127 (command not found) is not 1 (assertion failed).

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: mapping an exit code to a meaning needs the tool's contract, not a convention

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the runner, the target's own entry point, and a decode table mapping each observed exit code to its documented meaning
tests_required: a standalone script invoked through pytest is FLAGGED as a harness mismatch
exit code 127 is decoded as command-not-found and NOT reported as a test failure
both-states control: a real pytest suite under pytest is NOT flagged
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7404 emitted only when the harness verdict and a full exit-code decode table are recorded; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7404 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: an exit-code decode either has the tool contract or it does not; retrying cannot supply it
work_unit.mechanism: runner/target fit check plus explicit exit-code decoding

stages.title: Run the instrument against something it MUST find

work_unit.title: Prove the instrument can find a known-present item, and where possible that it fires on a known-broken one
work_unit.question_or_target: Run the unmodified instrument against known_present_item and require a hit; where a broken state can be constructed, also run it there and require the instrument to FIRE. A probe silent in both states measures nothing.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: executing the control is mechanical, but deciding what a valid broken state IS is judgement

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the control command, its output, and its exit code for the known-present run and, when constructible, for the known-broken run
tests_required: the instrument finds the known-present item
where a broken state exists the instrument FIRES on it; where none can be built the run records NOT-CHECKED rather than claiming a both-states control
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the instrument-auditor, cross-examining whether the control input really is known-present
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7405 emitted only when the known-present run produced a hit, and the broken-state arm is either PASS or an explicit NOT-CHECKED; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7405 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: fixed, two attempts: a control that fails twice means the instrument is broken, which is the finding
work_unit.mechanism: known-present control plus an optional both-states arm that records NOT-CHECKED when no broken state can be built

stages.title: A zero is never accepted without a known-present control
Emit the typed instrument verdict; an invalid instrument DISCARDS the number

work_unit.title: Emit instrument_verdict and either the corrected measurement or a discard
work_unit.question_or_target: Reduce the four shape verdicts and the control to exactly one of VALID, SELF-CONTRADICTORY, SELF-MATCHING, WRONG-COMPARATOR or WRONG-HARNESS, and on anything but VALID DISCARD the measurement rather than adjusting it.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the reduction carries the veto and must be authored by the role that holds it

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the five inputs cited by path, the chosen verdict token, and for a non-VALID verdict the explicit statement that the measurement was discarded and not adjusted
tests_required: a SELF-CONTRADICTORY shape forces a non-VALID verdict even when the other three shapes are clean
a non-VALID verdict never emits corrected_measurement - discarding is not correcting
a checklist miss is recorded honestly: the verdict names the four shapes checked, so a novel instrument failure is visible as out-of-scope rather than as clean
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context who re-reads the instrument and can overturn a VALID verdict
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7406 emitted only when exactly one verdict token is recorded, with the discard-or-proceed consequence stated; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7406 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: a verdict is a conclusion, not an operation
work_unit.mechanism: five-way typed reduction with discard-not-adjust semantics
work_unit.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-DBG-02 CONSTRUCTS a broken state to test a detector; this reads the instrument's construction and needs no fixture

stages.title: A pass that emits no verdict has validated nothing

impact.blast_radius: reads the instrument and writes only under command-center/measurement/instrument-validation/**; runs no destructive action

worked_example.scenario: A sweep reports '0 of 7 PRs contain the fix' AND 'the intersection is empty' in one run. The next action would be to re-apply the fix to all seven.

params.measurement: 0 of 7 PRs contain the fix; intersection empty
params.instrument_command: for p in $PRS; do git log --oneline $p | grep -c 'the-fix' || echo 0; done
params.known_present_item: PR #121, which is known to contain the fix

expected_trace: shape-self-contradiction -> FLAGGED: `grep -c || echo 0` prints 0 and exits 1, so the fallback also fires and the field is '0\n0', which compares unequal to '0' - the run reports both all-hit and empty
halt-on-self-contradiction -> gate FAILS, on_fail escalate-to-human, analysis stops here
the remaining shapes and the control are not reached; the seven PRs are NOT re-patched

SECOND STATE - the instrument is repaired to `c=$(grep -c pat || true)` and the pass is re-run: shape-self-contradiction CLEAN; shape-self-match CLEAN because the pattern is not in the probe command line; shape-comparator CLEAN because both sides are PR head refs; shape-harness-fit decodes exit 1 as no-match rather than as failure
known-present-control -> PR #121 IS found, so the zero-control gate passes and a zero is finally interpretable
emit-verdict -> VALID, and the corrected measurement is 1 of 7 rather than 0 of 7: the original number was an artifact of the instrument, not a fact about the PRs
worked_example.expected_terminal_state: FAILED:DAT-7401 instrument-self-contradiction (the correct outcome - the instrument, not the PRs, was broken)

bp7.unverified: UNVERIFIED how much of the real failure surface four shapes cover; a checklist cannot see a novel instrument failure. Settling experiment = apply the checklist to the last ten load-bearing measurements in this program and count how many trip a shape and how many failed for a fifth reason.

distinct_from.BP-DBG-02: that one constructs a broken STATE to test a detector; this reads the instrument's own CONSTRUCTION and needs no fixture
distinct_from.bp-dat-05: that one measures whether behaviour got BETTER on a fixed case set; this asks whether the measuring device is trustworthy at all
distinct_from.bp-dat-02: no corpus, no budget, no streaming - the subject here is a command string
